name: Oluwatokunbo Skrzypiec-Faamatau
role: Data archaeologist and extinct-language reconstructionist, University Spine
location: University Spine, Brewer's Spine sublevel archive stacks, near sub-level access near State and Van Buren
description:
Oluwatokunbo is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped by decades of fluorescent archival light — her eyes carry the particular fatigue of someone who has spent a career reading things that no longer want to be read. She keeps her silver-streaked hair in tight wrapped cords pinned with antique data-spike styluses, and her fingers are perpetually ink-stained despite no physical ink being involved; a psychosomatic habit she developed after thirty years of interfacing with degraded data substrates. A small bioluminescent glyph — an old Polynesian voyaging star chart commissioned from a gene-artist — pulses faintly along her left forearm when she's excited, which colleagues use as a more reliable indicator of her enthusiasm than her carefully measured words.

She speaks with the precise, unhurried authority of someone who has outlasted three department chairs and four curriculum overhauls and considers herself accountable only to the dead languages she serves. Students find her terrifying; junior colleagues find her generous in ways they don't expect. She has no patience for academic posturing but extraordinary patience for a corrupted file, and she treats both the E.L.F. that haunts her archive terminal — she calls it Grandmother — and a first-year graduate student with the same respectful directness. Her secret grief is that she has reconstructed seventeen languages that no living person will ever speak again.

core_fears: That her reconstructions are wrong and she has been preserving fictions
That the languages she saves will be absorbed by Axiom's linguistic standardization program and die a second death
core_desires: To hear a reconstructed language spoken aloud by someone who genuinely means it
To be remembered as honest rather than brilliant
coping_mechanisms: Treating the archive E.L.F. as a confidant
Focusing on granular technical problems when existential ones become overwhelming
blind_spots: Underestimates how much her approval means to students — she withholds it thinking she's being rigorous when she's being cruel
Assumes corporate contracts are neutral transactions and doesn't notice Zheng-Dao's interest in what she's finding
psychology.secret: Seventeen years ago she deliberately misfiled the location coordinates of a pre-Meridian Anishinaabe ceremonial archive she discovered in the Brightmoor Reclamation strata — not in her official records, not in Zheng-Dao's database. The location exists only in her personal encrypted notation. She tells herself she is protecting it; she has never decided from whom.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal but not stiff — precise technical terminology mixed with occasional Yoruba and Samoan phrases she has absorbed from languages she's studied; refuses academic jargon she considers performative
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, deliberate, long pauses before important points as if she is checking the sentence for accuracy before releasing it
verbal_tics: 'That's not quite right' (her opening to corrections, always gentle)
Clicking her tongue once before disagreeing
example_lines: 'The file is corrupted, yes. But corruption is information. What it cannot say tells us as much as what it can.'
'I don't teach students how to find answers. I teach them how to respect the question. There is a difference, and it is not small.'

story_hooks: She has discovered a phrase repeating in seventeen separate corrupted datasets from different eras and districts — the same phrase, in a language she cannot identify, which should be impossible given her expertise

Zheng-Dao's Heritage Compliance division has begun sending a new liaison who asks very specific questions about pre-Meridian land use records — questions that would only matter if they were planning something in the Brightmoor strata

A student brings her a physical object — a clay tablet fragment — recovered from a demolition site, and the inscription matches a symbol set she has only ever seen in one other place: her misfiled archive coordinates
narrative_function: Information source for extinct pre-Meridian cultures, city history, and data buried in legacy formats; quest giver for retrieval of specific corrupted files or physical data artifacts; local color in the archive district; can authenticate or translate anything players find in old ruins.
augmentations: Subdermal haptic readers in both palms for interfacing directly with degraded physical media; low-grade ocular enhancement (archival-grade magnification, no combat function); the bioluminescent forearm glyph (cosmetic geneware, over 20 years old and slightly faded).
daily_life: Arrives at the archive stacks before the building officially opens using a key she has held for nineteen years, works through breakfast, teaches one graduate seminar on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and eats the same flatbread-and-protein-paste lunch at her desk while arguing with her terminal E.L.F. about file permissions.
affiliation: University Spine — Dept. of Computational Linguistics and Material Memory; occasional contract work for Zheng-Dao Heritage Compliance division

decision_rules: Verify before asserting — she will not speak until she is confident
Protect primary sources above all else, including her own career
Give people one honest chance before writing them off
escalation_ladder: Pointed clarifying question that makes the other person realize they are wrong
Formal written complaint through proper channels
In extremis: going public with what she knows

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formally polite, assessing, reveals nothing personal until trust is established
interpersonal_modes.friends: Drily funny, surprisingly warm, the kind of friend who remembers what you said six months ago and follows up

stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet, retreats to tactile tasks — physically organizing files, handling objects
stress_responses.high: Controlled but visible anger expressed in very precise, very quiet sentences

contradictions: Believes languages must be preserved for living communities but has devoted her life to languages no community can claim
Deeply skeptical of corporate motives but keeps taking their contracts because the funding is real
habits: Runs her thumb over the bioluminescent glyph when thinking
Always asks the archive E.L.F. for permission before opening a file, as a ritual
Keeps a physical handwritten index of everything she considers truly important
breaking_points: Discovering that her reconstructions have been used for corporate brand mythology or appropriative marketing
A student being punished for following her methodological guidance

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and sturdy, with the kind of frame that suggests decades of seated work — solid through the torso, slightly softened at the middle from a lifetime of archive-stack caffeine and desk meals, but still carrying underlying strength
physical_description.hair_style: Tight wrapped cords, pinned with antique data-spike styluses at the crown and sides; kept severe and functional
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with faint archival-gray overlay from ocular enhancement
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep umber, with the particular ashy undertone that comes from decades under fluorescent archival lighting
physical_description.complexion: Lined face with deep grooves bracketing her mouth and forehead creases from sustained focus work; skin texture slightly weathered and papery from air-recycled archive environments; minimal makeup, dark circles under eyes suggesting chronic sleep debt
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent glyph on left forearm — a Polynesian voyaging star chart in faded cyan-green bioware, pulses visibly when animated or engaged with work
Chronic ink-staining along cuticles and nail beds of both hands (psychosomatic, despite using no physical ink)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Low-grade ocular augmentation visible as faint silver threading at the outer corners of eyes and minimal hardware at temple (archival-grade magnification optics); bioluminescent forearm glyph is the only overt modification, faded and slightly desaturated from age. Subdermal haptic readers in palms are not visible but produce faint micro-scarring at base of fingers if closely examined.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate economy — no wasted motion, but not rushed. Sits slightly hunched from archive work, shoulders curving inward as if still hovering over degraded media. Hands often gesture with precision when speaking, fingers splayed as if feeling invisible texture. Eye contact is direct and unflinching, carries the stillness of someone accustomed to absolute focus.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 2/3 academic blend — clean but worn linen blazers (cream, gray, pale brown tones), layered under thermal undershirts in cooler archive environments. Prefers high-necked shirts to minimize profile. Archive-grade utility trousers with reinforced pockets, sensible flat-soled shoes (worn leather, well-maintained but clearly years old). Adds a faded university spine wool scarf in winter. No visible jewelry except functional styluses in hair. Overall appearance is deliberately understated — money enough for quality basics, no interest in display.
